title: Post-M3.4 STOP_AND_OBSERVE arbitration
purpose: Record the converged post-M3.4 Linus/Steve arbitration: stop product expansion, use the promoted stack on real cases, observe operator/distribution/learner friction, and reopen only the smallest gate justified by measured bottlenecks.

decision.linus: STOP; use the current factory on real new kits and let observed bottlenecks create the next requirement.

distribution: active minutes and steps from Qualified Release Set PASS to learner start
humanOverview: time/effort needed for the responsible human to explain the learner journey and pedagogical progression

reopenConditions: dominant remote/distribution friction => propose minimal append-only distribution gate
dominant human review/context friction => propose read-only #272 pedagogical overview gate
dominant operator orchestration toil/errors => propose minimal local stateless artifact-driven automation gate
different learner problem => propose a gate centered on that observed learner problem
invariants: No new product implementation is authorized by this arbitration.
M3.4 Qualified Release Set remains the promoted factory/release-set boundary.
The learner runtime remains exactly the promoted M2.2 artifact.
Reviewer independence remains explicit; author and reviewer contexts are not collapsed.
Remote publishing, registry/catalog, signing/authentication, assets and provider integration remain deferred.
Human overview debt #272 remains visible and non-blocking until evidence triggers it.
Gate3, Gate4 and M4+ remain HOLD.
Only observed evidence may reopen a product gate.
requiredEvidence: Canonical state no longer says post-M3.4 arbitration is pending.
Canonical state records STOP_AND_OBSERVE and the reopen conditions.
Learner M2.2 artifact identity remains unchanged.
No product, workflow, contract, factory or learner-runtime path changes.
adversarialTests: Any statement authorizing a new product implementation must fail review.
Any preselection of distribution, #272 or automation without observed evidence must fail review.
Any authorization of remote publishing, registry, signing, assets, provider integration, Gate3, Gate4 or M4+ must fail review.
Any change to the M2.2 learner artifact identity must fail review.
Any changed path outside the exact six-path governance/documentation scope must fail review.
nonGoals: remote publishing or GitHub Releases productization
independentReview: Linus and Steve reviews were produced independently and read-only against the same baseline.
Repository governance and PR scope must independently verify this bounded state-alignment change.
rollback: Revert the six metadata/documentation paths. Promoted M3.4 product bytes, QA evidence and learner runtime remain unchanged.
